corrections.proposed: unset until sources agree: 12.2 m (40 ft) or 15.2 m (50 ft)
corrections.why: 3.0 m matches no tower height in any source; the Register describes a 50 ft steel tower and Forest Lookouts a 40 ft tower, and the 14 by 14 ft cab is not the tower height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 50 ft in the Register, firelookout.com and the state record; 40 ft in Forest Lookouts and Cheryl Hill. Height left unset in facts.
Forest Lookouts dates an arson burning to 1995; the Register and state record say vandals destroyed the 1956-era steel tower in 1996; Cheryl Hill says arsonists in 1996. The story gives all three.
State record says rebuilt in 1956 and Cheryl Hill says a new steel tower in 1956; the Register says the older tower was upgraded in 1958. The story reports 1956 and notes the Register's date.
Register gives a 14 by 14 ft flat-top cab; Forest Lookouts gives 15 by 15 ft with a wood cab. Both reported.
Register 5,165 ft; firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill 5,210 ft; state record 5,200 ft. The current record's 1,574.3 m matches the Register and was left unchanged.

notes_for_editor: The 3.0 m height in the record is wrong (see corrections). Heights (40 vs 50 ft), cab size and cause and year of loss (arson 1995 vs vandals or arson 1996) conflict across sources, so the story reports the disagreement. A 1937 newspaper line describes the old tower as 50 feet above the rocky top, which does not square with the 30 ft 1934 tower named by the Register and firelookout.com; not reconciled. Current staffing rests on undated firelookout.com plus the June 2022 visit. Access is recorded as permission because the gate sign on Green Diamond land grants revocable recreational use; no public-entry rule for the tower was found.
